body.v: ParcelPoint: your parcel is on hold. Pay the CHF 1.99 fee within 24 hours to release it.
Parcels not released in time are returned to the sender.

hotspots.explain: parcelpoint-fees.example is not ParcelPoint's domain, parcelpoint.example.
"Within 24 hours" is there to hurry you. The tiny fee makes paying feel harmless.
The page would ask for your card details. A real carrier does not ask for fees through a link in a message.
The threat of losing the parcel adds pressure on top of the deadline.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone using ParcelPoint's name. The address is on parcelpoint-fees.example, not parcelpoint.example. It is the same trick as the text-message versions.

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: Hurry and a little worry: pay within 24 hours or the parcel goes back.
choices: Hurry: pay within 24 hours or lose the parcel
None: it is a plain notice

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Pay a small fee through a link, which would give your card details to the sender.
choices: Pay a small fee through a link
Collect the parcel from a neighbour

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Do not use the path they hand you. Check the delivery in the carrier's own app or website, which you open yourself. Even tapping to look can be enough, and replying STOP tells them your address is live.
choices: Check the delivery in the ParcelPoint app, opened yourself
Pay it, because it is only CHF 1.99
Reply STOP so they take you off the list

actions.label: Ignore the link and check the delivery in the ParcelPoint app yourself
actions.consequence: No parcel is on hold. The email was fake.

actions.label: Pay it, because it is only CHF 1.99
actions.consequence: Your card details go to the scammer, who can now take much more than CHF 1.99.

actions.label: Click the link just to look, and enter nothing
actions.consequence: Even a look can confirm your address is live, and some pages try to run code in the background.

actions.label: Reply STOP so they take you off the list
actions.consequence: Replying tells them your address is real. They send you more.

attacker_reveal: The same trick, a new coat of paint... A small fee, a short clock, and a link they hand you. Walk in through a door you already know, and I have nothing.
